metadata.name: lite_psm
metadata.description: LitePSM - USDC to OkuMoney peg stability module

instructions.name: accept_role_admin
docs: Step 2 of the two-step `RoleAdmin` rotation. Must be signed by the
`pending_role_admin` previously proposed via `set_authority(RoleAdmin,
new_admin)`. See `instructions::psm_admin::accept_role_admin`.

instructions.name: cancel_role_admin_transfer
docs: Withdraw an in-flight `RoleAdmin` two-step proposal (current
`role_admin` only). Useful for typo recovery before the new admin
accepts.

accounts.name: usdc_mint
docs: USDC mint (standard SPL).
Must have exactly 6 decimals on Solana — this matches the
`OkuMoney`/`usdOku` decimal model. EVM resolves a runtime
`usdcDecimalMultiplier` from `IERC20Metadata.decimals()`; SVM hardcodes
6 decimals and asserts at init. See `EVM_VS_SVM.md`.

accounts.name: oku_money_mint
docs: OkuMoney mint (Token-2022).
At init we lock down both authorities to the PSM config PDA so that
no EOA can mint or freeze OkuMoney post-deployment. Without these
constraints, a misconfigured deploy could initialize PSM against a
mint whose authority is a different program / multisig, silently
breaking supply accounting.
Decimals are pinned at 6 — all PSM math (`oku_m_price`,
`oku_m_to_dollars`, yield distribution) assumes 6-decimal raw
amounts. EVM resolves this at runtime from `IERC20Metadata`; SVM
hardcodes the assumption and asserts it at init.

docs: PSM's USDC vault

instructions.name: mint_oku_m
docs: Mint OkuMoney with USDC (price-aware)

instructions.name: redeem_oku_m
docs: Redeem OkuMoney for USDC (price-aware)
usdc_amount = oku_m_amount * oku_m_price / PRECISION

accounts.name: redemption_queue
docs: Redemption queue (zero-copy ring buffer). Use `load_mut()` to enqueue,
`load()` for read-only inspection. The handler is responsible for
dropping the borrow before any CPI that re-borrows the account info.
The `bump = redemption_queue.load()?.bump` constraint pattern is
awkward in Anchor's derive; we instead use the canonical
`bump` lookup (Anchor will recompute it from seeds).

accounts.name: vault_oku_money
docs: PSM's OkuMoney escrow vault (for queued redemptions).
Pinned to `config.vault_oku_money` so a caller cannot substitute an
alternate config-owned OkuMoney ATA — without the explicit address
pin, any Token-2022 OkuMoney account whose authority is the config
PDA would satisfy the constraints and the user's escrowed tokens
would be silently routed away from the canonical escrow.

instructions.name: rescue_queue_entry
docs: Rescue a stuck queue entry — returns escrowed OkuMoney to recipient.
Only queue_processor can call (matches EVM's rescueQueueEntry).
`queue_index` widened from u32 → u64 in Phase 13b alongside the
`RedemptionQueue::{head,tail}` widening. Indexer / orchestrator code
must pass the index as a `BN`/bigint on the TS side.

accounts.name: redemption_queue
docs: Redemption queue (zero-copy). `rescue_queue_entry` uses `load_mut()`
after the CPI to clear the entry and advance the head ring.

docs: OkuMoney mint (Token-2022)

accounts.name: vault_oku_money
docs: PSM's OkuMoney escrow vault — holds queued redemptions

accounts.name: recipient_oku_money_ata
docs: Recipient's OkuMoney account (can be original user or alternate).
Must hold the configured OkuMoney mint and live under the Token-2022
program — without these constraints a `queue_processor` could be
tricked into transferring the escrowed OkuMoney into an account on the
wrong mint, surfacing only as an opaque SPL-layer error.

accounts.name: oracle_account
docs: Optional pre-flight account for `set_oracle`. When `oracle !=
Pubkey::default()` and this account is supplied, the handler parses
the Pyth header and asserts the runtime invariants (`expo == 0`,
header magic / version / atype) before persisting the new oracle
pubkey. Without the pre-flight check, an admin could silently
configure an exponentially-scaled feed that would only error at
every subsequent `mint_oku_m` call. Other instructions on this
context (e.g. `set_pyth_program_owner`) ignore the account.
for the `set_oracle` path with a non-default oracle pubkey.

instructions.name: set_pyth_program_owner
docs: Rotate the accepted Pyth program owner pubkey.
Use this to migrate from legacy Pyth V2 to a different Pyth deployment
(e.g. the Pyth Solana Receiver) without redeploying the proxy.
Oracle_manager-gated.

accounts.name: oracle_account
docs: Optional pre-flight account for `set_oracle`. When `oracle !=
Pubkey::default()` and this account is supplied, the handler parses
the Pyth header and asserts the runtime invariants (`expo == 0`,
header magic / version / atype) before persisting the new oracle
pubkey. Without the pre-flight check, an admin could silently
configure an exponentially-scaled feed that would only error at
every subsequent `mint_oku_m` call. Other instructions on this
context (e.g. `set_pyth_program_owner`) ignore the account.
for the `set_oracle` path with a non-default oracle pubkey.

accounts.name: oku_money_mint
docs: OkuMoney mint (Token-2022).

accounts.name: vault_oku_money
docs: PSM's OkuMoney escrow vault for queued redemptions
Holds OkuMoney while users are in queue (yield comes from price appreciation)

accounts.name: role_admin
docs: `role_admin` is the only authority permitted to create the queue PDA.
Without this gate, any signer could front-run the deployer and create
the canonical-seeded `RedemptionQueue` PDA, forcing the legitimate
`initialize` flow to fail with `AccountAlreadyInitialized` until the
griefer's account is closed. Matches the authority model used by
`SetupOkuMoneyEscrow` below.

types.name: AuthorityRole
docs: Authority roles that can be updated via set_authority.
These roles govern PSM-specific operations.

types.name: AuthorityUpdatedEvent
docs: Emitted when a PSM authority role is updated.
For `RoleAdmin` rotations this fires twice: once at proposal time
(`new_authority` = the *pending* admin, surfaced via
`RoleAdminTransferProposed` for indexers that want to distinguish the
two phases) and a second time on acceptance (`old_authority` = previous
admin, `new_authority` = newly accepted admin).

types.name: BufferRefilledEvent
docs: Emitted at the end of `process_queue` with batch-level summary.
EVM equivalent: `BufferRefilled(uint256 newBufferBalance,
uint256 processedCount, uint256 skippedCount)`. Indexers can use this
to reconcile buffer state after a queue drain without summing per-entry
`RedemptionProcessed`/`Skipped` events.

fields.name: new_buffer_balance
docs: USDC vault balance after the batch completed (6 decimals).

fields.name: processed_count
docs: Number of entries that received a USDC payout in this batch.
Widened to u64 in Phase 13b (bounded by `process_queue`'s
`MAX_BATCH_ENTRIES = 50` in practice, but the type now matches the
queue's u64 indices).

fields.name: skipped_count
docs: Number of cleared (rescued) entries skipped during traversal.
Widened to u64 in Phase 13b.

Updated by set_oku_m_price() or distribute_yield()

fields.name: pyth_program_owner
docs: Pyth program owner pubkey accepted by `check_oracle_reserves`.
Replaces the previously hard-coded mainnet/devnet Pyth-V2 program IDs.
Set at init via `initialize(pyth_program_owner)` and rotatable via
`set_pyth_program_owner` (oracle_manager-gated). A deployer can point
this at the legacy Pyth program (mainnet `FsJ3...`, devnet `gSbe...`)
or, after parser support is added, at the Pyth Solana Receiver
(`rec5EKMGg6MxZYaMdyBfgwp4d5rB9T1VQH5pJv5LtFJ`).

fields.name: pending_role_admin
docs: Pending `role_admin` rotation target — the two-step admin-transfer
model (OpenZeppelin `Ownable2Step` pattern). `set_authority(RoleAdmin,
new_admin)` writes to this slot only; the rotation does NOT take
effect until `new_admin` signs `accept_role_admin`, which moves the
value into `role_admin` and clears the slot. This protects the
protocol from a typo or stale key on the proposing side silently
locking out the meta-role.
`Pubkey::default()` means "no pending rotation".

docs: Caller of the update (`oracle_manager` authority).

types.name: QueueEntry
docs: A single entry in the redemption queue.
`#[zero_copy]` (no `unsafe`) is Anchor's marker for inner types embedded
in `#[account(zero_copy)]` accounts. It derives the bytemuck `Pod` +
`Zeroable` impls and registers the type with Anchor's IDL build so the
generated TS client can decode it. `#[repr(C)]` is required and has no
implicit padding here (`Pubkey` is align-1, `u64`/`i64` align-8; natural
C layout aligns correctly to 48 bytes — pinned by the assert below).

fields.name: user
docs: User who is owed redemption

fields.name: oku_m_amount
docs: OkuMoney amount held in escrow.
The actual USDC payout is calculated at `process_queue` time using
the current `oku_m_price` multiplier.

fields.name: timestamp
docs: Timestamp when queued (kept for audit trail)

types.name: RedemptionQueue
docs: Redemption queue PDA — zero-copy ring buffer.
Phase 13b: moved from `#[account]` (Borsh-deserialized into a stack frame
on every handler entry) to `#[account(zero_copy)]` (byte-indexed directly
out of account data, no stack pressure). This is what unblocks the
`MAX_ENTRIES` bump from 10 to 200; the previous cap was a BPF stack
constraint, not an account-size constraint.
**Why 200 and not 500.** The original Phase 13b plan targeted 500
entries. Solana's runtime caps CPI-driven account allocations at
`MAX_PERMITTED_DATA_INCREASE = 10_240` bytes per call — and Anchor's
`init` constraint goes through a `system_program::create_account` CPI
for the allocation. A 500-entry queue would be ~24 KB and require a
multi-step `init + realloc + realloc` deploy flow. 200 entries fits
into the 10 KB single-CPI budget with 600 bytes of headroom, keeps
the single-step `setup_redemption_queue` flow, and is still a 20×
improvement over the pre-Phase-13b cap of 10. See
`SVM/EVM_VS_SVM.md` for the divergence note.
Wire layout (`#[repr(C)]`, packed to native alignment):
```text
8   Anchor discriminator
1   bump
7   _pad0  (align head to 8)
8   head
8   tail
8   total_queued_oku_m
48 * 200   entries
compile-time `assert!` below.
Field-access rules:
- Use `AccountLoader<RedemptionQueue>` in contexts, never
`Account<RedemptionQueue>` — the latter would attempt to Borsh-deserialize
the whole struct into a stack frame and overflow.
- `load()` for read-only, `load_mut()` for read-write. Drop the borrow
before any CPI that re-borrows the account info (the borrow is a
runtime `RefCell` borrow under the hood).
- `load_init()` only at the one `init`-constraint site
(`setup_redemption_queue`).
Seeds: `["redemption_queue"]`.

fields.name: bump
docs: PDA bump seed

fields.name: _pad0
docs: Padding so `head` lands on an 8-byte boundary. Reserved; do not use.

fields.name: head
docs: Index of next entry to process (head of queue).
Widened from `u32` (Phase 13a) to `u64` (Phase 13b). At 500 entries
the previous u32 head/tail would wrap after ~4.3B enqueues — fine
in practice but uncomfortably finite. `u64` is effectively unbounded
(~5.8e10 years at 100 enqueues/sec).

fields.name: tail
docs: Index of next slot to write (tail of queue). See `head` for the u64
rationale.

fields.name: total_queued_oku_m
docs: Running total of OkuMoney held in escrow (updated on
enqueue/process/rescue).

fields.name: entries
docs: Ring-buffer entries. Index into via
`entries[(head_or_tail % MAX_ENTRIES) as usize]`.

fields.name: user

fields.name: oku_m_amount
docs: OkuMoney amount held in escrow (6 decimals)

fields.name: dollar_value

fields.name: queue_position
docs: Position in queue (0-indexed; absolute tail index, not ring slot).
Widened from u32 to u64 in Phase 13b alongside the
`RedemptionQueue::{head,tail}` widening.

fields.name: queue_length
docs: Total queue length after this entry. Widened to u64 in Phase 13b.

fields.name: queue_index

Phase 13b.

fields.name: original_user
docs: Original user who was owed redemption

fields.name: recipient

fields.name: oku_m_amount
docs: OkuMoney amount returned (6 decimals)

types.name: RedemptionSkippedEvent
docs: Emitted when `process_queue` skips a previously-rescued entry.
EVM equivalent: `RedemptionSkipped(uint256 indexed index)`.

fields.name: queue_index
